transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2025-08-27 15:30 PDT
- Duration: ~47 minutes
- Attendees: Avery Chen, Samir Patel (Redwood); Maya Lopez, Ethan Park, Ruth Kim, Jonas Berg, Priya Singh (HaloHealth)

Summary:
Quick renewal check-in focused on upcoming capacity uplift (20% baseline + burst), adding EU region with private VPC option, and contract amendment timeline. Customer raised questions on latency targets versus cost, KMS options for key management, and SOC2/audit evidence. SE to run EU baseline throughput tests and Redwood AE to send pricing amendment.

Topics:
1) Current consumption & growth profile
2) EU region onboarding (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC)
3) Latency SLOs and cost tradeoffs (batching / quantization options)
4) Security & compliance artifacts (SOC2, KMS, RBAC)
5) Contract amendment and timing

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, um, quick roll call then we'll jump in. Maya?
[00:06] Maya (HaloHealth): Hey all, Maya here.
[00:08] Ethan (HaloHealth): Ethan on the line.
[00:09] Ruth (HaloHealth): Ruth, security.
[00:10] Jonas (HaloHealth): Jonas here.
[00:11] Priya (HaloHealth): Priya - SRE.
[00:13] Samir (Redwood SE): Samir, Redwood SE.
[00:15] Avery: Cool, thanks. So we sent a short pre-read earlier — pricing + proposed EU activation plan — did everyone get that?
[00:22] Maya: Yes, skimmed it. Haven't fully digested the burst examples.
[00:25] Ethan: Got it. Quick context — we've been seeing about a 18% month-over-month QPS growth, with spikes during nightly inference windows. We're looking to secure a renewal and add EU region for data residency.
[00:37] Avery: Understood. High level, the ask was: renew for another 12 months, base capacity +20%, and EU region activation as either hosted EU or private VPC depending on compliance. Also optional burst credits for Blackbox weekends, correct?
[00:49] Maya: Yeah that's it. Also we want clearer KMS boundaries and the audit logs retention.

[02:10] Samir (Redwood SE): On the EU side there are three paths — hosted EU (fastest), Dedicated EU cluster (reserved GPUs, lower latency), or Private (VPC/on-prem) which is the most isolated. Tradeoffs: hosted = fastest time-to-activate but shared tenancy; dedicated = predictable latency at cost; private = full control but longer lead time.
[02:35] Ruth: For us, we need the option to bring keys into our KMS, some form of HSM or BYOK. Is that possible?
[02:42] Samir: Yep we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated; hosted can use envelope encryption with customer keys in some cases — we'll share the exact network diagram.
[02:52] Maya: And egress — how does EU traffic route? We want to avoid cross-border egress for PHI.
[02:58] Jonas: Specifically, the model endpoints need to be inside EU region to meet our legal counsel's ask.

[05:00] Samir: For EU residency we can provision model endpoints in eu-west-1 cluster and optionally set routing so EU requests never leave the region. If you want full control we can do VPC peering and on-prem connectors; that'll be part of the private deployment checklist.
[05:18] Priya: Ballpark lead times?
[05:20] Avery: Hosted EU is ~5 business days to flip on and validate. Dedicated EU depends on capacity commit — around 3 weeks for reserved pool provisioning. Private on-prem is variable, typically 6-8 weeks plus network setup.

[07:30] Ethan: Latency is a big concern. Our front end has a 150ms P95 target. Can Redwood hit that with dedicated?
[07:38] Samir: For short sequences and small models dedicated single-GPU endpoints can get under 100ms P95, but it depends on model size and token length. We can profile with your real payloads — recommend a microbench with the KV-cache patterns.
[07:56] Maya: We do a lot of long-chat prompts for clinical summarization, so sequence length is often 512–1k tokens.
[08:03] Samir: For that range the KV cache behavior matters; batching helps throughput but will increase tail latency. There's a knob in Redwood Optimize for per-route batching and latency windows.

[12:30] Jonas: On cost: we need the math showing cost per 1M tokens for dedicated vs hosted with burst. The pricing sheet was confusing about amortized GPU costs.
[12:40] Avery: Absolutely — we'll send an updated pricing table that shows unit economics for your observed distribution: baseline 24/7 traffic vs nightly spikes. We'll include burst credits and a 'burst pricing multiplier' example.
[12:53] Ethan: Can you include an example where quantization reduces cost by 30% but increases infer time by 10ms?
[12:59] Samir: Sure — we have quant profiles (int8, 4-bit) and we can surface expected latency and quality deltas per model. We'll attach those to the pricing sheet.

[20:45] Ruth: Security checklist: SOC2, ISO, audit logs retention, SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS, and support for external auditors. We need to confirm what evidence you can share for our compliance team.
[20:58] Avery: We'll share the SOC2 report and the security pack. For auditors we can provide syslog streams, long-term audit logs (custom retention), and a network diagram. For Private deployments, we can show HSM screenshots / KMS integration evidence.
[21:15] Ruth: Great. Also, contractually, we want an SLA clause for regional failover and a fallback to hosted if dedicated goes down.
[21:24] Avery: That can be part of the amendment — automatic fallback policy and crediting for unavailable capacity. We'll loop legal.

[28:00] Maya: Timeline question — if we sign the amendment by Sep 2 can we have EU hosted activated by Sep 10?
[28:08] Avery: Hosted yes, that's doable. Dedicated will take longer — we'd need the capacity commit and then schedule provisioning; realistic target mid-late Sep. Private will slip further.
[28:20] Jonas: We may start with hosted EU and then move to dedicated once we finalize budgets.
[28:24] Samir: That's a common path: hosted for fast residency, then dedicated for latency SLAs. We'll prepare a migration checklist.

[35:10] Ethan: Benchmarks — we'd like Redwood to run a throughput test using our sample payloads. Can SE have access to sample traces? We'll need NDAs?
[35:20] Maya: We can sanitize traces, remove PHI.
[35:23] Ruth: We'll need a data handling agreement.
[35:26] Avery: Fine — we'll get legal copies ready. For the benchmark, Samir can run a baseline on the eu-west cluster and push results into the shared benchmark sheet.
[35:37] Samir: Yep. I'll ask for the sanitized traces and run the KV-cache microbench and the batching profiles; we'll share raw numbers and a summarized readout.

[42:50] Priya: Operationally, during spikes we want an autoscale policy that prioritizes latency-sensitive routes and throttles background bulk jobs. Is that available?
[42:58] Samir: Yes, you can define per-route SLOs and route policies. There's also graceful degradation: route to smaller model variants or to cached responses. We'll show the console config.
[43:12] Maya: Awesome. One last question — competitors: we benchmarked ZetaAI and CloudRunAI; Zeta had slightly better short-seq latency but higher cost. Anything Redwood wants to call out?
[43:26] Avery: Our differentiator is predictable economics and transparent tradeoffs (batching, caching, quantization). We'll include a short comparative note in the pricing packet.

[46:00] Avery: OK let's recap action items...
[46:05] Maya: Quick recap is great.
[46:07] Avery: Action items — we'll send updated pricing with burst scenarios, Samir will run EU microbench after we get sanitized payloads, Ruth will confirm KMS scope, Jonas will share QPS growth numbers. We'll aim to have a draft amendment by Aug 31 and target activation of hosted EU by Sep 10 if amendment signed.
[46:30] Ethan: Sounds good.
[46:33] Ruth: Thanks everyone.
[46:35] Avery: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links to the pricing sheet, SOC2 pack, and the benchmark tracker.
